direct_answer: Pets give company and a reason to move, but dogs pulling on leads and pets underfoot can cause falls. Training, the right lead, help with walks and planning ahead can make pet ownership safer.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
Pets can be good for wellbeing.

This guide covers staying safe. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Dog walking

  • Use a lead that does not wrap around your hand.
  • Consider training for pulling.
  • Walk on even paths.

Indoors

Watch for pets underfoot; use a night light.

Help with care

Charities and neighbours may help with walks.

Planning ahead

Arrange who would care for your pet if you are unwell.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is a dog good exercise?

It can be.

What if I cannot walk them?

Ask for help.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: 5 steps to mental wellbeing
